title: 材料力学
subtitle: Strength of  Materials
teachers:
OGURI Kazuyuki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: Strength of Materials clarify the forces and deformations of various parts of bridges, towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, etc. These results can be used for design safety. It is an important subject that forms the basis of mechanical engineering. In this course, students should gain a thorough understanding of the basics of the strength of materials through lectures and practice. Students will explore examples of structures in the community where material mechanics is utilized, and will also make effective use of generative AI.
advice:
Students must thoroughly learn the following as the necessary basic knowledge for engineers at any stage of their career.
It is important to work through many exercise answers, but the study of strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand by just memorizing formulas and patterns. For all problems, students will start from an understanding of the basic formula and solve the problem by setting appropriate boundary conditions for the problem.

1. Stress and strain, 2. Hooke’s law, 3. Mechanical properties of materials, 4. Allowable stress and safety factors,
5. Frame structure, 6. Thermal stress, 7. Stress concentration,
8. Thin-walled cylinder subjected to internal pressure,
9. Beams and their supporting conditions, 10. Shearing force and bending moment of a beam,
11. Stress on beams, 12. Deflection of beams

Furthermore, students should understand the real applications of structure by applying strength of materials in their locality.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Unspecified
Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand the course Industrial Mechanics I. Students need to fully understand the content of this course as the basis of the courses Mechanics of Aircraft Structure and Design of Aircraft Structure in later semesters.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain and Hooke's law.
Be able to explain deformation and fracturing behavior of materials by drawing stress-strain characteristics.
Be able to explain relationship between material properties, reference strength and the allowable stress.
Be able to explain stress in frame structure and thermal stress, and also explain stress concentration.
Be able to explain the shearing force and bending moment occurring in a beam by drawing SFDs and BMDs.
Be able to determine the stress and deflection occurring in a beam and to design safe structures.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Understand the concepts of stress and strain.
2. Distinguish nominal stress and true stress, nominal strain and true strain.
3. Conduct safe design using standard strength and allowable stress.
4. Calculate stress in frame structures and thermal stress.
5. Draw SFDs and BMDs of all beams.
6. Calculate bending stress and deflection of beams and achieve safety in designs.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Calculate stress and strain.
2. Perform calculations with safety factors in mind.
3. Calculate thermal stress.
4. Draw SFDs and BMDs of beams.
5. Calculate bending stress and deflection of simple beams.
